$comment: Things this classroom does not want the game to ask for.
Put a target in `ignore` and no dot will ever ask for it. The octopus does
NOT lose that dot — the geometry is locked at 107 and never moves. The dot
is given a different challenge of the same kind instead, so the drawing is
identical and only the question changes.
WHAT TO WRITE. Exactly what the game asks for:
a shortcut    "COPY"  "PASTE"  "CUT"  "UNDO"  "REDO"  "SAVE"
"FIND"  "BOLD"  "SELECT ALL"
WHEN YOU WANT THIS.
- The key does not exist on your keyboards. A US (ANSI) board has no key
between Left Shift and Z, so < and > cannot be typed on it at all.
- The combination fights something else on your machines, or the class is
not ready for it yet.
- You want a shorter, easier round for younger children.
`add` works the other way: a target listed there is brought INTO the game.
It takes its turn from whatever is repeated most, so nothing disappears and
the dot count never changes.
Leave the list empty to play the full curriculum. Save the file and reload
`at` pins a target to a numbered dot, for something a class wants to end on.
the page; there is nothing to rebuild.
